description: Seok Bum Hong and colleagues publish a probabilistic model of train-driver human error with its parameter and output data. The September 2026 ZIP archive contains Python code, seventeen input distributions, link coefficients and three deterministic case configurations. It documents Latin-hypercube Monte Carlo sampling with 300,000 iterations, one-at-a-time and Sobol sensitivity analyses, thresholds and parametric intervals. Input sources are listed in a provenance CSV. Code is MIT-licensed and data and outputs use CC BY 4.0, with free access. The model can explore how assumptions affect human-error probabilities in railway safety simulations. Its cases do not establish field-calibrated failure rates across railway systems; empirical transferability remains unknown. The describing manuscript is identified as submitted. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Reported runtimes and reproduction tests were not independently checked.
